newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ZAMBIA KONKOLA DEEP STUDY SEEN COMPLETE BY END-'97.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA KONKOLA DEEP STUDY SEEN COMPLETE BY END-'97.

text.p: Due diligence and feasibility studies into the Konkola Deep copper project in Zambia should be completed by the year end, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday.
Chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said in his annual chairman's statement that investigations into the project were now under way and were expected to be completed by the end of 1997.
A consortium led by Zambia Copper Investment Ltd (ZCI), which is 50.6 percent owned by Anglo, signed a memorandum of understanding with the Zambian government in February this year.
ZCI's other partners in the project were Gencor Ltd and Falconbridge Ltd, but Gencor surprised analysts by withdrawing in May.
The consortium said earlier this year that it would cost between $700 million and $800 million to develop the Konkola Deep mine -- seen as pivotal to the future of Zambia's copper industry.
The mainstay of the country's mining industry at present, the Nchanga open pit mine, is expected to run out of ore at the end of the century.
